activities.caption: one line of the mix-consistency summary is wrong
activities.name: mktConsistencySpot

config.prompt: One line of this marketing-mix summary is wrong. Find it.
lines: The four Ps must tell the same story
A premium product sold through discount chains sends contradictory signals
Contradictions are fine as long as the price is high enough
A budget airline and a flag carrier differ in four coordinated Ps
config.correction: Contradictions are never fine — the four decisions must be coordinated, or the signals cancel each other.
config.why: Audi and Rolls-Royce differ not in having 'a price' but in four coordinated Ps — and the same holds for the budget airline and the flag carrier.

activities.anchor: A logistics company's software saves a mid-size warehouse
activities.caption: call the value price — not the cost price
activities.name: mktValueEstimate

config.prompt: Cost-plus logic suggests 300 a month. The software saves the warehouse about 4,000 a month — roughly what does value-based logic charge?
config.why: 1,200 a month — still leaving the customer 2,800 of net benefit, while quadrupling revenue: the negotiation becomes about sharing the value, not recovering the cost.
config.context: Hermann Simon's blunt finding: most firms systematically underprice, because cost is knowable and value requires research.

activities.anchor: a retention improvement is worth more than most acquisition campaigns
activities.caption: call the retention multiplier
activities.name: mktChurnEstimate

config.prompt: A customer pays 20 a month at 70 per cent gross margin with 2.5 per cent monthly churn — LTV 560. Cutting churn to 1.9 per cent lifts LTV to roughly what?
config.why: About 737 — and a retention problem cannot be fixed with more acquisition, which is why retention is the multiplier most teams underfund.
config.context: The rule of thumb: LTV/CAC of 3 or better, with CAC recovered within about a year.

activities.anchor: The honest denominator charges everything acquisition actually consumed
activities.caption: true or false — what CAC really measures
activities.name: mktCacJudge

statements.s: CAC is just the advertising spend divided by new customers.
statements.why: The honest denominator charges everything acquisition consumed — commissions, promotions, free trials, agency fees, growth-team salaries.

statements.s: The numerator counts new customers won, not purchases — many purchases are existing customers returning.
statements.why: Counting returning customers flatters the machine and hides the leak.

statements.s: A firm computing CAC from media spend alone will conclude its unit economics work years before the accounting agrees.
statements.why: That is how teams talk themselves into burning cash.

statements.s: Free trials and sales commissions do not belong in CAC.
statements.why: They are acquisition costs like any other — the all-in number is the honest one.
